about: Calques and false friends commonly found in English written by speakers of French, each with the form to use instead. The list is based on errors that speakers of French are generally known to make, and is not yet confirmed by errors found in real use. "find" is a case-insensitive regular expression. It must match "example", which contains the error, and must not match "correct".

calques.why: French "actuel" means "current". In English, "actual" means "real", as opposed to "supposed".
calques.example: Install the actual version of the plugin.
calques.correct: Install the current version of the plugin.

calques.why: French "actuellement" means "currently". In English, "actually" means "in fact".
calques.example: Only two formats are actually supported.
calques.correct: Only two formats are currently supported.

calques.why: French "éventuellement" means "possibly" or "if necessary". In English, "eventually" means "in the end".
calques.example: Eventually we can add a second reader.
calques.correct: If necessary, we can add a second reader.

calques.why: French "assister à" means "attend". In English, "assist" means "help".
calques.example: The owner assisted at the review.

calques.why: French "préciser" is a verb meaning "specify". In English, "precise" is only an adjective.
French "dans le cadre de", translated word for word, gives "in the frame of". In English, the phrase is "as part of".
calques.example: In the frame of the release we updated the guide.
calques.correct: As part of the release we updated the guide.

calques.why: French "réaliser" means "carry out". In English, "realize" means "become aware of", and only rarely "achieve".
calques.example: We realized the migration in two steps.
calques.correct: We carried out the migration in two steps.

calques.why: French "dépendre de", translated word for word, gives "depend of". In English, "depend" is followed by "on".
calques.example: The result depends of the configuration.
calques.correct: The result depends on the configuration.

calques.why: French "évolutions" means "changes" or "new features". In English, "evolutions" is rarely used in that sense.
calques.example: The release notes list the evolutions of the plugin.
calques.correct: The release notes list the changes to the plugin.

calques.use: "for" before a length of time, "since" before a point in time
calques.why: French "depuis" is followed by a length of time. In English, only a point in time follows "since", and a length of time follows "for".
calques.example: The test has failed since three days.
calques.correct: The test has failed for three days.

calques.use: information, advice, software, feedback, equipment, knowledge, hardware (no plural)
calques.why: In English these nouns are uncountable and have no plural. The plural is copied from the writer's own language, where the corresponding nouns are countable.
calques.example: The log keeps all informations about the run.
calques.correct: The log keeps all the information about the run.

calques.use: what it looks like, or how it looks
calques.why: English uses either "what … looks like" or "how … looks". "How … looks like" mixes the two, following the pattern of the writer's own language.
calques.example: The page shows how the report looks like.
calques.correct: The page shows what the report looks like.
